review.title: The algo's call
review.body:
Logged before the start, last snapshot Nov 20, 12:47 AM ET. It had Wellington 49%, the draw 27% and Western Sydney 23%, projecting Wellington 1.5 – Western Sydney 1 (2.5 total, Wellington by 0.6).

Final: Wellington 2 – Western Sydney 0. Right winner: it had Wellington at 49%.

review.title: How the ratings held up
review.body:
Wellington came in with a 28% above average attack and a 15% stingier than average defense (2-1-2, 1.4 scored and 1.2 allowed a game over 5 games), worth about 24 and 24 games of evidence. Projected to score 1.5, they scored 2 (+0.5 goals, 30% over); projected to allow 1, they allowed 0 (−1 goals, 100% under).

Western Sydney came in with a 11% below average attack and a 13% leakier than average defense (2-0-1, 1.7 scored and 0.7 allowed a game over 3 games), worth about 23 and 22 games of evidence. Projected to score 1, they scored 0 (−1 goals, 100% under); projected to allow 1.5, they allowed 2 (+0.5 goals, 30% over).

The bigger miss was Western Sydney's scoring (-1 goals against projection).

review.title: Where the result sat in the simulations
review.body:
Total: 2 against 2.5 projected (-0.5), about the 38th percentile of the simulated totals (a typical game swings ±1.7).

Margin: Wellington by 2 against Wellington by 0.6 projected, about the 19th percentile of the simulated margins (typical swing ±1.7).

An ordinary result: inside the range the simulations expected most of the time.

review.title: Situational factors, checked
review.body: Nothing situational moved this projection (rest, travel, form and conditions were all normal), so it came down to team strength.

review.title: Against the market
review.body:
WSW ML (+425) at +425: the algo gave it 18% vs 18% fair (+0.4 pts) — lost (-1u); beat the close (closing fair chance 22%). Draw (+350) at +350: the algo gave it 21% vs 20% fair (+0.4 pts) — lost (-1u). WEL ML (-205) at -205: the algo gave it 61% vs 62% fair (-0.9 pts) — won (+0.5u); beat the close (closing fair chance 78%). WSW PK (-110) at -110: the algo gave it 49% vs 50% fair (-1.3 pts) — lost (-1u). WEL PK (-110) at -110: the algo gave it 51% vs 50% fair (+1.3 pts) — won (+0.9u). OVER 2.5 (-155) at -155: the algo gave it 55% vs 56% fair (-0.7 pts) — lost (-1u); same number as the close. UNDER 2.5 (+110) at +110: the algo gave it 45% vs 44% fair (+0.7 pts) — won (+1.1u); same number as the close.

The line barely moved between the algo's snapshot and the close.

No bet: nothing cleared the algo's bar before the game.

review.title: What could have made it wrong
review.body:
Flagged going in: early-season numbers were thin; inputs were missing (WEL lineup rating or past seasons, WSW lineup rating or past seasons).

The projection landed within its normal range anyway, so the flags didn't cost it much this time.

review.title: What the algo learns
review.body:
This game's own lesson: scoring came in at ×0.788 of the raw projection, and the home side beat its projected margin by -1.5 goals. It counts toward Soccer scoring level, home edge and both teams' attack and defense corrections.

Across 1361 graded Soccer games the algo now scales scoring ×0.940 and gives home teams -0.1 goals. Team corrections start after 3 graded games for a team.

review.title: Bottom line
review.body: Right side, total within its normal range, margin within its normal range, no bet.
